subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps - Lumos Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps - Lumos Health

Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

High-level pain points you called out:
- Heavy inference spikes during patient intake windows (roughly 9–11am ET and 3–5pm ET).
- Must isolate PHI and meet strict data-residency requirements (US-only).
- Current SLA gaps: 99th pct latency spikes to 600–800ms under load; need consistent sub-200ms for core flows.
- Procurement timeline: target contract in place by end of May so you can start onboarding in June.

Goals we discussed:
- Provide dedicated GPU capacity (reserved) with network/isolation controls so Lumos can process PHI-sensitive workloads.
- Deliver predictable throughput: baseline 1,000 inference requests/min with bursts up to 4,000 reqs/min.
- Achieve latency SLOs: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms for primary model endpoints.
- Support staging and scale plan for seasonal peak traffic; automated burst capacity to avoid throttling.

Proposed Redwood Dedicated configuration (initial recommendation):
- Reserved capacity: 4x A100-equivalent GPU nodes (isolated tenant pool in us-east-1).
- Burst/auto-scale footprint: up to 8x nodes during peak (policy-based scaling with warm standby).
- Networking: VPC peering + customer-managed subnets, KMS integration for keys.
- Ops/SLA: SLA target 99.9% availability for reserved capacity; 30-minute paging for Sev1 incidents, runbook-driven on-call rotation.
- Security: SOC 2 controls, audit logs, and optional on-prem connector if required for air-gapped processing.

Attachments I’m sending: Lumos_Dedicated_SOW_draft.pdf (draft SOW outlining capacity, term, and responsibilities) and capacity_runbook.xlsx (technical runbook + scaling policies). I’ve also included a preliminary pricing_estimate_v1.xlsx for budget planning.

Ask/next steps:
1) Please confirm that the above pain points and goals are captured correctly.
2) Can you confirm target start date for provisioning (we recommended early June)?
3) If procurement is OK, we’ll circulate the SOW for redlines and schedule a technical kickoff with Ethan and Dylan next week.

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for a 30-minute technical kickoff. Thanks — appreciate the candid conversation today.

—

Alex — quick technical notes to address your Qs and give you something to share with procurement.

Cost ballpark:
- Estimated monthly run-rate (4x reserved A100-equivalent + ability to burst to 8x): USD $78k–$110k, depending on term length, committed usage discounts, and whether you add the premium SLA. I’ll mark this as preliminary — we can provide a formal quote once term length and data egress assumptions are set.

Lead time:
- Typical provisioning: 7–10 business days after SOW + security questionnaires complete for us-east-1 dedicated pools. If you opt for pre-warmed standby nodes, we can shorten initial warm-up to 3–5 business days.

SLA & compliance:
- Availability SLA for dedicated pools: standard 99.9% (we can offer 99.95% with an enhanced SLA addendum and additional reserved capacity).
- SOC 2: we can provide the attestation and a security package (certificate + controls mapping). We’ll include standard data-retention controls and logging — we can bake specific retention terms into the SOW.

Technical runbook highlights (see attached capacity_runbook.xlsx):
- Autoscale policy: CPU/GPU utilization + qps thresholds with KV cache priming to reduce cold-start latency.
- Batching strategy: dynamic batching with a 30ms batching window for throughput-sensitive flows.
- Fallbacks: automatic route to a lower-cost model variant in case of capacity exhaustion, with circuit-breaker alerts to your ops team.
- Monitoring & observability: per-route tracing, p99 latency dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns in Redwood Console.

If the above sounds right, I’ll prepare a short MOU to lock capacity and circulate the SOW for procurement review. Marissa — I’m available Wed Apr 14 at 10am ET for the tech kickoff. I’ll bring the runbook and a slide with expected token/sec and latency projections.

—Ethan
